response.title: which 3d printer filament dryer actually dries filament the best
response.answer:
If your priority is which filament dryer actually removes the most moisture, rather than which has the best features, I'd focus on three things:

Actual filament temperature: Can it reach and maintain 70–85°C throughout the spool, not just at the heater?

Moisture removal: Does it actively exhaust humid air instead of trapping it inside?

Air circulation: Does it heat the entire spool evenly, including the inner windings?

This matters especially for nylon (PA), PA-CF, PC, and other engineering filaments. A dryer that reaches 70°C on its display isn't necessarily drying the filament at 70°C.

My top picks for actual drying performance
Shop
Best proven drying performance

SUNLU FilaDryer S4

70°C maximum · 4 spools

In MyTechFun's standardized water-removal test, it removed approximately 100% of the test water in 30 minutes. That's among the strongest documented results in the comparison. 
mytechfun.com

SUNLU FilaDryer E2, Up to 110℃, Professional Drying and Anne…

110°C advertised maximum · 2 spools

The strongest high-temperature capability on paper, especially for nylon and PC. However, independent testing has raised concerns about temperature overshoot and uneven heating, so I wouldn't call it the proven winner. 
SUNLU
+1

SUNLU FilaDryer S4 Pro, Dual-Zone Filament Dryer with Indepe…

$139.99 · 85°C maximum · 4 spools

Promising upgrade to the S4, with two independently controlled heating zones. But there's not yet enough comparable independent testing to establish whether it dries better than the original S4.

Creality SpacePi X4 Filament Dryer (Live Exclusive)

$149.00 · 85°C maximum · 4 spools

Another strong high-temperature candidate, with two independently heated chambers. Independent moisture-removal comparisons remain limited.

What the actual testing shows

One useful independent comparison is MyTechFun's filament dryer tests. It measures how quickly each dryer removes water from a standardized wet sponge.

These results measure evaporation from a sponge, not moisture removed from the interior of a filament spool. They are useful for comparing heating and ventilation, but they don't establish which dryer is fastest for saturated nylon.

My recommendation

For PLA, PETG, TPU, and ABS, I'd choose the SUNLU S4 based on its measured performance.

For PA-CF, nylon, PC, or PPA, I'd investigate the SUNLU E2, but only after confirming the exact hardware revision and its temperature stability. A high-temperature dryer that overheats parts of the spool can cause problems.

One question that would change my recommendation significantly:
